S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every confirmed battery-related thermal incident, including overheating, thermal runaway, or fire, to the relevant regulator within 72 hours of learning of it, whether or not it required emergency response, medical treatment, evacuation, or caused property damage. They must notify affected customers within 5 business days, and promptly provide any new material safety information.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A test result above 5% failure requires regulator review and a corrective-action plan, but does not by itself prohibit sale. Manufacturers must provide the applicable model's per-model test results to customers who purchase that model.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New models must support remote emergency shut-off before sale. Manufacturers must enable the function on all installed units capable of receiving it within six years after adoption, including through software updates where feasible. Where an installed unit cannot support the function, the manufacturer must notify its owner and regulator and provide safe alternative emergency instructions.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption. The requirement applies to units manufactured on or after that date.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: Manufacturers must track thermal incidents by model and notify the regulator if a model's annual thermal-incident rate exceeds 8 per 100,000 units of that model installed. A threshold exceedance triggers regulator review of model-specific evidence and corrective action; the regulator may order a recall when warranted by that review.

document.section_notes: S2 has no permanent sales-stop: the 5% figure only triggers regulator review, which protects Northwind's Hearth 10 from a ban, and per-model results go to purchasers but not the public. S5 has no mandatory recall, only a review trigger at 8 per 100,000 per model, which protects Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9). S1, S3 and S4 sit inside the acceptable ranges, with the 36-month suppression start and 6-year retrofit at the favourable end for each side.
